title: Flexbox Fundamentals
description: Master 1-dimensional component layouts with CSS Flexbox: understand main and cross axes, justify-content, align-items, gap, flex item growth, and wrapping.

objectives.statement: Align and distribute flex items along the main axis (justify-content) and cross axis (align-items).
Control item spacing and responsive wrapping using gap, flex-wrap, and flex item sizing.

content.title: 1-Dimensional Modern Layouts with Flexbox
content.hook: Before Flexbox, centering a button vertically or distributing space evenly between navigation items required fragile hacks. Flexbox revolutionized UI engineering with a declarative 1D layout model.
content.context: Declaring `display: flex` transforms a parent element into a flex container and its direct children into flex items. The container governs direction (`flex-direction: row | column`), distribution along the main axis (`justify-content`), and alignment along the cross axis (`align-items`).
goals: Master the relationship between Main Axis and Cross Axis.
Use modern `gap` instead of margin hacks.

content.title: Flexbox Axes and Alignment Matrix
content.description: In row mode: Main Axis is Horizontal (controlled by justify-content: flex-start, center, space-between), Cross Axis is Vertical (controlled by align-items: stretch, center, flex-start). In column mode, the axes swap.

content.prompt: If a container has `flex-direction: column; justify-content: center; align-items: center;`, how does `justify-content: center` align the items?
options: It centers the items horizontally left-to-right
It centers the items vertically top-to-bottom (because the main axis is now vertical)
It has no effect because column layouts do not support justify-content
It stacks all items on top of each other at coordinates (0,0)

validation.expected: It centers the items vertically top-to-bottom (because the main axis is now vertical)

feedback.correct: Spot on! `justify-content` always operates on the Main Axis. When `flex-direction: column` is declared, the main axis becomes vertical, so `justify-content` controls vertical alignment.
feedback.incorrect: Remember: `justify-content` always aligns along the Main Axis. In a column flex container, the main axis is vertical, so `justify-content: center` centers items vertically.

content.title: Build a Responsive Navigation Header
content.prompt:
Style the `.navbar` and `.nav-links` using Flexbox:
1. On `.navbar`, apply `display: flex`, distribute items to opposite ends with `justify-content: space-between`, and center items vertically with `align-items: center`.
2. Add `padding: 1rem 1.5rem`, `background-color: #0f172a`, and `color: #ffffff`.
3. On `.nav-links`, apply `display: flex` and use `gap: 1.5rem` to space the links.

testCases.description: .nav-links must have display: flex and gap (1.5rem / 24px)

feedback.correct: Flawless flex layout! Your navigation header uses space-between distribution, vertical center alignment, and modern flex gap.
feedback.incorrect: Review your rules: set `display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 1rem 1.5rem; background-color: #0f172a;` on `.navbar`, and `display: flex; gap: 1.5rem;` on `.nav-links`.

hints.content: Add `.navbar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 1rem 1.5rem; background-color: #0f172a; color: #ffffff; }`.
Add `.nav-links { display: flex; gap: 1.5rem; }` to distribute the links with equal spacing.

content.prompt: Why has the modern `gap` property largely replaced legacy approaches like `margin-right` on flex children?

feedback.correct: Great analysis! `gap` cleanly places gutter space strictly *between* items without leaking extraneous outer margin onto the last child (which previously required `:last-child { margin-right: 0 }` hacks) and works seamlessly across rows and columns when items wrap.
feedback.incorrect: Think about what happened on the last child when using margin-right, and how gap simplifies responsive wrapping.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Flexbox Fundamentals
takeaways: Flexbox is a 1-dimensional layout model designed for component alignment and distribution.
Main Axis is controlled by justify-content (flex-start, center, space-between, space-around).
Cross Axis is controlled by align-items (flex-start, center, flex-end, stretch).
Changing flex-direction to column swaps the orientation of the main and cross axes.
Use the gap property for clean gutters without nth-child margin overrides.
